title: Counting in 3s, forwards and backwards

accuracy.evidence: Checked on 26 Nov 2026 against the National Curriculum in England (2013) mathematics programme of study, Year 2 Number and place value statutory requirement 'count in steps of 2, 3, and 5 from 0, and in tens from any number, forward and backward', and the Year 3 follow-on (count from 0 in multiples of 4, 8, 50 and 100). Every number in the lab and items was checked in code: the 3s count 0-30 (TRI.inCount), the gap lines 3, 6, [9], 12, [15], 18 and 30, 27, [24], 21, [18], 15, 6 tricycles x 3 = 18 wheels, cards 12, 21, 27 in the count and 13, 20, 23 not, and every parameterised answer (3k+3 for k 1-8, 3k-3 for k 2-10, 3t for t 2-7) at its corners.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented skip-counting slips (Fuson 1988 on counting-on errors, where children count the start number as 'one'; NCETM counting and place value materials on skip counting as counting equal groups): counting the start stone (hop-of-2 feedback 'Do not count 6 itself: say 7, 8, 9'; challenge tag 'start'; m3 'He counted the start number'), counting on in 1s or 2s (tag 'ones', distractor 10 after 9), going up when counting back (back-hop feedback and tag 'back'), thinking numbers ending in 3 are in the 3s count (13 and 23 cards, tag 'three'), and saying the number of groups instead of the total (6 tricycles prediction, tag 'groups').

lab_distinct.evidence: The mechanism is a frog hopping exactly 3 along a sliding window of a 0-30 number track, with a hop arc labelled +3 or -3 for each landing and a full 0-30 line underneath that fills in landing dots; the canvas checks hop size and direction on every tap or frog drag. Then a forward and a backward 3s line with gaps to drag tiles into, tricycles counted in 3s, and a lands-on/hops-over sort. No other lab hops in 3s both ways or diagnoses hop size; flag_skip (2s, 5s, 10s), flag_sixes and flag_fours use different mechanisms, and the lab_distinct gate passes.

lab_teaches.evidence: Children find the landing stone themselves (a wrong stone names the hop size and lists the three stones to say), so the 'over two, land on the third' rule is discovered on the track before the text confirms it; the overview line shows the evenly spaced landing dots; the back hop reverses the same rule; the gap lines force 'what is 3 more / 3 less'; the tricycles link the count to equal groups, and the final sort shows that only numbers you say are in the count.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'Yes, it lands on 10' (the frog goes 9, 12 and hops over 10), '21' or '14' for a back hop from 18 (the frog goes back to 15, not up and not a hop of 4), and '6' wheels for 6 tricycles (the count ends on 18). The reveal text after each task names what the learner predicted.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions with answers in rotating positions; every wrong option carries a slip tag with its own message: 'ones' (that counts in 1s or 2s), 'start' (do not count the number you start on, from 9 say 10, 11, 12), 'back' (counting back makes numbers smaller), 'three' (ending in 3 does not put a number in the 3s count), 'groups' (that is how many tricycles, count the wheels in 3s).

readability.evidence: validate_lessons.py passes; the kid text scores about FK grade 0.7 (target 5) and the adult text about 8.0 (target 10). Kid sentences are short with concrete words (hop, stone, frog, wheels, tricycle). Canvas instructions are one short line each ('Hop in 3s from 0. Where does the frog land?'), and number labels on the canvas are 18-26 px for ages 6-7.

no_filler.evidence: Every kid paragraph teaches one part: add 3 each time; a hop goes over two and lands on the third, do not count the start; counting back takes 3 away; counting groups of 3 and the last number is the total; ending in 3 does not make a 3s number. The adult notes give the curriculum statement, the bridge to the 3 times table, named mistakes and what the lab does. The filler gate passes.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at iPhone 13 (390 px) in light and dark and on desktop for every step before and after Show me. Fixes made from screenshots: the stones jumped down when a reply line appeared (now fixed at 42% of the canvas height), the track step had empty space (added the 0-30 overview line) and the tricycle read as a scooter (now a side view with a visible far wheel and a seat). Stones are about 43 x 49 px and tiles, gaps and cards at least 56 px tall on a phone.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin with a descriptive aria-label ('Make the frog hop from 9 to 12', 'Put 15 in the next gap of the counting on line', 'Count tricycle 3: 3 more wheels', '13 goes in Frog hops over it'); the canvas aria-label is updated live with each reply and step description; the challenge uses real buttons with a polite live region; axe WCAG 2.1 AA runs in both themes in the browser gate.

sources: DfE (2013) National Curriculum in England: mathematics programmes of study, Year 2 Number and place value ('count in steps of 2, 3, and 5 from 0, and in tens from any number, forward and backward') and Year 3 Number and place value
NCETM (2017) Mastery Professional Development materials: Number, Counting and Place Value (skip counting and counting equal groups)
Fuson, K. C. (1988) Children's Counting and Concepts of Number. New York: Springer (counting-on errors, including counting the start number)
